name: phantomkit — Scanner, Package Manager and Supply-Chain Gate
one_line_value_proposition: One dependency-free tool for static analysis, secret scanning, an npm-compatible package manager and a signed supply-chain gate.
buyer_problem: Security gating is usually split across a scanner, a package manager, an audit tool and a registry, each with its own trust assumptions and install footprint.
solution_summary_public: phantomkit combines a rule-based scanner (SARIF output, autofix, taint tracking), an npm-registry-protocol package manager with secure defaults, a file-backed private registry, and a CI gate that binds lockfile, audit and scan results into a signed attestation.
differentiators_public: Runs on the Python standard library only — no runtime dependencies to vet.
Secure-by-default installs: dependency install scripts are not run, git/URL dependencies are rejected, lockfile host and integrity are verified.
Gate fails closed when no advisory source is reachable, and emits an attestation that can be re-verified.
verified_capabilities: 113 bundled scan rules and 27 secret detectors, each with annotated fixtures; `verify.sh` reports 110 fixture checks passed, 0 failed, and 0 findings in a self-scan (run 2026-10-15).
Semgrep-style rule syntax including taint mode, SARIF 2.1.0 output, baselines, diff scanning and autofix.
npm-compatible install/ci/audit/sbom/publish with package-lock.json (v2/v3) interoperability and CycloneDX/SPDX output.
Private registry with scoped tokens and a hash-chained audit ledger; `pk gate` produces an HMAC-signable attestation.
unverified_claims: Parity with Semgrep or npm beyond the limits stated in the project README (the author lists these limits).
Registry behavior at scale or under hostile network conditions.

public.headline: Gate your builds on code, dependencies and secrets with one standard-library Python tool.
public.subheadline: phantomkit scans source with Semgrep-style rules, installs npm packages from a verified lockfile, serves a private registry and emits a signed attestation of the result.
public.cost_of_inaction: Unverified lockfiles, install scripts and typosquatted dependencies are a known supply-chain attack path. This is a qualitative statement; no statistic is cited.
public_limitations: Token-structural matching, not a full AST; intra-file taint only; the bundled ruleset is far smaller than commercial registries.
No lockfile v1 support; simplified peer-dependency resolution; registry is single-node.
Source repository is private and shows a single visible commit; contributor history was not reviewable.
architecture_public: Scanner engine + YAML rule loader → findings (text / JSON / SARIF).
Resolver + lockfile writer + content-addressed cache → install / ci.
Gate: lockfile verify + audit + license policy + scan → signed attestation.
public.risk_summary: Scope limits listed above; private-repository provenance and contributor history unreviewed; no revenue or customers.
